--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_margulis_gabber_galil_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Add the Margulis-Gabber-Galil expander on an n x n torus. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_margulis_gabber_galil_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Add the Margulis-Gabber-Galil expander on an n x n torus. title: >- [Graph.add_margulis_gabber_galil_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Add the Margulis-Gabber-Galil expander on an n x n torus. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add the Margulis-Gabber-Galil expander on an `n x n` torus. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19390-L19530){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_margulis_gabber_galil_graph( n, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Margulis-Gabber-Galil graph](../assets/graphs/add-margulis-gabber-galil-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Margulis-Gabber-Galil graphs on the n by n grid of coordinate pairs modulo n. Each point (x, y) is joined to eight images under fixed affine maps, so every node has degree 8 counting self-loops, drawn as small loops, and repeated pairs, drawn bowed apart: n=2 and n=3 on a ring, and for n=4 the 4 by 4 grid with only the eight edges of the point (1, 1) shown, in the accent color, reaching its images such as (1, 3) and (3, 1)." width="100%"} Creates the `n^2` nodes `(x, y)` with `x` and `y` taken modulo `n`, and joins each node to four images under fixed linear maps of the torus: `(x + 2y, y)`, `(x + 2y + 1, y)`, `(x, y + 2x)` and `(x, y + 2x + 1)`. Every node sends four edges and receives four, so the graph is 8-regular, and its second-largest adjacency eigenvalue stays below `5 * sqrt(2) ≈ 7.07` for every `n`: it was the first explicit family of expanders (Margulis 1973, made effective by Gabber and Galil 1981). Some images coincide with the node itself or with each other, so the graph has self-loops (counting `2` toward the degree) and parallel edges. It is NetworkX's `margulis_gabber_galil_graph()`. Nodes are created row by row (`x` then `y`), and with `label=True` each is labelled `"(x,y)"`. In a directed graph every edge points from a node to its image. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Margulis-Gabber-Galil graphs are useful for: - explicit, deterministic expanders for testing mixing, routing and error-correcting constructions - comparing spectral gaps of structured and random regular graphs - sparse graphs where random walks mix quickly at every size ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Side of the torus. Must be non-negative; the graph has `n^2` nodes and `4 n^2` edges. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each node is labelled with its torus position as `"(x,y)"`. Because these labels don't depend on the existing nodes, adding a second labelled torus raises `ValueError`; pass `label=False` for it. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is negative. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~add_grid_graph`) : Join each point of a grid or torus to its neighbors. [](`~add_chordal_cycle_graph`) : Build another explicit expander, on a cycle. [](`~is_regular_expander`) : Check the spectral expansion of a regular graph. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a 5 x 5 torus there are 25 nodes and 100 edges, and every node has degree `8`: ::: {#ee2ae86e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_margulis_gabber_galil_graph(n=5) degrees = set(graph.degrees(return_dict=True).values()) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges(), degrees ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (25, 100, {8}) ``` ::: ::: The origin maps to itself under two of the maps, giving two self-loops: ::: {#21f3d9d2 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} origin = graph.get_id_from_label("(0,0)") edges = graph.get_edges_as_tuples() [graph.get_label_from_id(t) for _, s, t in edges if s == origin] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['(0,0)', '(1,0)', '(0,0)', '(0,1)'] ``` ::: ::: ### Maps or neighbors The same 25 points of a `5 x 5` torus, at their grid positions. On the right, the torus from `add_grid_graph()` joins each point to its four grid neighbors, with the wraparound edges drawn across the grid. On the left, the Margulis–Gabber–Galil maps send each point to points far across the grid, which brings every point within fewer steps of every other: ::: {#068795ce .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} torus = ec.Graph().add_grid_graph(dims=[5, 5], periodic=True) pos = {i + 1: [i // 5, i % 5] for i in range(25)} for g in (graph, torus): g.set_node_attrs("pos", pos) graph.diameter(), torus.diameter() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (3, 4) ``` ::: ::: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#2d0ccb82 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.plot( layout="pos", show_labels=False, node_size=7, width=320, height=320, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
